did: Opened Talleyrand's Assess the Situation; he advised 'Satisfy their design (Britain)' (high confidence) - offer what Britain wants at the table. I clicked that recommended button, then 'Propose peace' on the generic standstill dialog it opened.
expected: A way to offer Britain something for 'The Low Countries' design (satisfy their design), priced and explained before I commit; or at least a note that peace is hopeless now.
saw: The button opened a generic 'war with Britain is at a standstill - Propose peace / Press advantage / Wait' box with a large empty body and no mention of the design or of odds. Choosing Propose peace silently spent 3 of my 5 DP on a plain Peace Treaty to Britain (the Cabinet had called such an offer 'Hopeless' for Austria). The advised action and the thing that happened did not match.

did: Clicked End Turn on turn 1 after beating Mack at Swabia, chasing him to Munich and capturing him there.
expected: No warning, or a warning about a real enemy. Mack had fled Swabia and then been captured (2,739 left, 1,369 escaped home).
saw: Warning: '2 corps stand in peril - an enemy force of ~29,126 shares the field (Swabia). Press End Turn again...'. 29,126 is exactly Mack's strength after the first battle; the map shows no enemy piece in Swabia (only my Davout +3). It looks like a stale figure for an army that is gone.

did: Clicked End Turn on turn 2 after beating Archduke Charles at Franconia (he was driven off, 'flees to Tyrol').
expected: No peril warning for a field the enemy had left.
saw: Again: '2 corps stand in peril - an enemy force of ~16,772 shares the field (Franconia)'. 16,772 is exactly Charles's remaining strength after the battle that drove him out to Tyrol. Same stale-enemy warning as on turn 1; it makes me doubt the warning when a real one comes.

did: Read the Turn 6 Morning Dispatch after vassalising Bavaria and signing a non-aggression pact with Prussia.
expected: Nothing about a war with those two courts; I have never been at war with either (Bavaria was my ally, now my vassal; Prussia is at peace with me).
saw: A dispatch line: 'Sire - the war with Bavaria and Prussia is over. Davout, Murat and Ney hold under your own orders and were not moved - the treaty offers a road, it does not overrule the Emperor. Their passage lapses with the corridor.' It made me think I had somehow been at war with my own vassal and with Prussia; it reads like a leftover of the right-of-passage mechanic and names the wrong parties.

did: Opened the Cabinet (F1) to reach a court, many times over the campaign (Austria, Britain, Russia, Prussia, Bavaria, Spain).
expected: A way to jump to a named court, or a window big enough to show the nation list.
saw: On the 5120x1440 screen the Cabinet is a small window showing about five lines; the list of nations is long (At War, Treaties, Vassals, Neutral...), so every visit is F1, then scroll the wheel (and again for the Neutral group, 20 notches), then click the court. The list order also changes as treaties change (Britain moved from At War to the bottom of Neutral), so I could not rely on where a court sat.

did: On turn 7 I paid 1,116g + 1 DP to buy off Britain's design and 1,152g + 1 DP for Russia's (the Balance of Europe page said buying off 'puts the design to sleep 15 turns'), and later 1,008g + 1 DP for Austria's. On turn 11 I read the Balance of Europe page again.
expected: Britain and Russia to be listed as kept out of the next league for the sleep, or the page to say plainly what the buy-off does and does not change.
saw: The Dispatch says 'Britain and Russia would now join a league against us' and the Balance page still lists both as 'she would join', pricing the way out at the same relations road (8 and 7 turns of Talleyrand) as before the buy-off (9 and 8), only a turn shorter. So about 2,300g bought one turn off a road I cannot afford anyway, while the wording 'the design sleeps 15 turns' reads as if the court is out of it. I also could not tell from the page which of my buy-offs was still in force.

did: On turn 3 I proposed an armistice to Austria (51 of 50, 'Favorable'). The preview said 'Bavaria stays at war with Austria under this truce ... 7 French corps stand on Bavarian soil'. I sent it, it was accepted, and I ended turns.
expected: A truce that stops the fighting where my corps stand, or a clear warning that my ally could be attacked while my corps are barred from helping her.
saw: On turn 4's enemy phase Archduke John attacked Munich and Swabia (Bavaria's soil), the garrison was destroyed and both provinces passed to Austria. My corps in Swabia (Ney, Davout, Murat) were then on 'Austria's soil under an armistice' and the game itself put them 'on the road home to Franche-Comte' (Berthier's order, not mine); Massena in Munich was told no corps of ours may enter it again. I lost two Bavarian provinces I had just fought for and my marshals were moved away without a command from me. The preview line was one bullet among many and did not say any of this.

did: Opened Bavaria's counter-offer to my vassalage proposal (I had sent 'France pays 142 gold').
expected: A counter that shows what changed from my terms.
saw: 'Revised Terms: You pay Bavaria 142 gold at the signing; You pay Bavaria 100 gold at the signing.' It did not say the 100 was the new demand, and the 154 gold a turn of tribute in my first draft was gone with no word. I could only tell by adding the two lines (242 gold went out). The report on the turn line called them 'France offers 142 gold / France offers 100 gold'.

did: Read Talleyrand's assessment of Austria during the armistice (turn 6, relations -66, mission running at +8 a turn).
expected: A projection that agrees with the armistice rule printed on the peace preview ('peace if relations have healed to -60 or better').
saw: It said 'relations stand at -66 and will thaw to -57, short of the line; the war resumes' - yet -57 is better than -60. A turn later the same page said the truce 'ripens into peace' at -57. The -57 also leaves out my own +8 a turn mission (it was only the natural thaw). I could not tell whether to trust the first wording.

did: On turn 4 I granted Prussia the licence against Hanover ('no gold, 1 diplomatic point') and ended up declining to stop the war on turn 10.
expected: The confirmation box to list what the licence costs me besides the stated 1 DP.
saw: The box talked only of reneging (-25 relations). On turn 11 the dispatch said 'Prussia has declared war on Hanover - relations with every court, France's included, fall 15', my Prussia relations dropped from +18 to +2 (my courting mission showed '-15 from Prussia's declaration'), and every court's relations fell. Nothing before the licence said that a successful licence lowers everyone's opinion of me.

did: Ended turn 1, turn 2 started with the enemy phase box, I clicked Continue and tried to open the Cabinet.
expected: To be able to treat with courts.
saw: The Cabinet button was greyed: 'a letter stands unanswered: the Cabinet stays shut until it is answered'. The letters were three envoys (Prussia, Ottoman Empire, Portugal) listed only as a number on a top-bar button, and I did not know the Cabinet and the letters were tied together until the tooltip said so. It happened every turn envoys arrived.

did: Started Improve Relations with Prussia on turn 1, then sent a (hopeless) peace letter to Britain the same turn; on turn 4 I looked at the Prussia page.
expected: Prussia relations to have moved about +8 a turn.
saw: Relations were -2 after four turns: the line read '+8 earned; paused 2 turns on your errand'. Every proposal I send makes Talleyrand carry it and pauses his mission, but nothing at the moment of sending says 'this stops the Prussia mission'. It repeated on turns 3 and 14 (the Hesse courtship paused 1-2 turns each time I sent anything).

did: On turn 2 I opened the settlement table with Austria and pressed Back Out; the log said 'Settlement draft kept. Reopen Settlement to continue editing.'
expected: The draft to still be there.
saw: On turn 3's start the log said 'Your unratified settlement draft with Austria (1 clause) was set aside at turn's end.' So 'kept' lasted only until I ended the turn, and the same word is used both times.

did: After the battle picture I pressed Escape to close it, then pressed T to open the Ledger (the game says bare keys work when you are not typing).
saw: The command line held the caret again, so a 't' was typed into it (command line shows 't') and nothing opened. I had to press BackSpace and use Alt+T. It happened every time a battle picture or a pop-up was closed with Escape.

did: Ended turns 7 to 20 with no enemy at war with me (only the Austrian truce, then full peace).
expected: No 'enemy phase' box when nothing happened.
saw: Every turn an ENEMY PHASE modal appears with one line, 'Britain, Russia, Austria and 6 other courts stirred, but their formations remain beyond our sight', and I must click Continue before anything else. It is the same sentence each time, even when I am at peace with all of them.

did: Opened the Cabinet page for Spain, my only treaty ally, whose relation was sliding (+40 on turn 1, +36 on turn 5).
expected: To be able to reassure her.
saw: Talleyrand: 'Reassure Ally is shut while Talleyrand is at Austria's court - recall Talleyrand first'. With one Talleyrand on one mission at a time I could not both court Prussia/Austria/Hesse and keep Spain warm; Spain slid to +23 by turn 18 (list label 'Neutral') and I never got a turn to reassure her.
